answer: A practical sybil defense for an agent economy is a reputation-weighted attestation chain: before agents can forge new transactions, each one must have a unique identity anchored by live peers. Imagine a mesa where every newcomer is vouched for by an existing agent who stakes its own standing on the introduction, and repeated endorsements cluster like a grove rather than a field of clones. A duplicate identity then costs more than it earns, since its vouching lineage collapses if fraud is proven, so mass account creation stops being profitable.
